bullets.content: Keep file work out of the shell: use Read with offset and limit instead of head, tail, or sed -n; Grep instead of grep; Glob instead of find and ls; Edit instead of sed -i; Write instead of heredocs and echo redirection.

Default to single quotes for shell text; put node -e, pwsh -Command, and python -c code in single quotes so the outer pwsh does not expand dollars, and write anything longer than one line to a file with the Write tool and run it by path.

Use -LiteralPath for any file name you did not make yourself, because -Path treats brackets, star, and question mark as wildcards; quote native glob patterns for programs with -g instead of letting the shell expand them.

Start a server with cmd.exe redirecting to logs/server.log and read the log tail, never pipe a server into Select-Object and never use Start-Process for servers; check $LASTEXITCODE yourself because a failing program never stops the script.

Bash habits fail on this pwsh with is not recognized or parser errors: grep, head, tail, wc, sed, awk, find, touch, seq, xargs, date -u, VAR=value prefixes, export, for-do loops, and heredocs all need their pwsh form from the pairs table.

Double-quoted dollars need braces or subexpressions: "$name: x" does not parse so write "${name}: x", "$o.a" prints the object so write "$($o.a)", "price $450" loses the number so use single quotes, and a backslash never escapes a quote.
The double-ampersand chain works only between two commands in pwsh 7 and never after foreach, if, or while; after a statement use a semicolon with if ($?) instead of &&.

Native traps lie quietly: plain diff compares file names not contents, find is the old Windows find.exe, curl means Invoke-WebRequest so write curl.exe, powershell is 5.1 so write pwsh, /c/ paths fail so write C:/, and a here-string opener must end its line with the closer starting its line.
